newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Hollywood finds foreign partners--paper.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Hollywood finds foreign partners--paper.

text.p: Italy's film studio complex Cinecitta has found partners for a newly-created operating company in an effort to keep the world's most famous movie studios outside Hollywood afloat and still producing films.

Milan financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore reported on Sunday that the holding company Ente Cinema, which hands down annual government grants to Cinecitta, will hold a 20 percent stake in a new company called Cinecitta Servizi to run the studios, while the studios themselves remain in state hands.

According to the newspaper, Italy's state broadcaster RAI and television and advertising group Mediaset will both take a 20 percent stake each in Cinecitta Servizi, while film producer Vittorio Cecchi Gori's company Fin.Ma.Vi will have 10 percent holding, a consortium of independent producers 10 percent, and British leisure company Rank Organisation Plc 20 percent.
